member.summary: Determines if a token is exchangeable based on its claims. An exchangeable token is one that is not a user token and has an audience claim that contains the appId of the token.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.Authentication.AgentClaims.GetAppId(System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt.JwtSecurityToken)
member.summary: Gets the appid from the given JWT token. This method checks the 'ver' claim to determine whether to look for the appId in the 'appid' claim (for v1 tokens) or the 'azp' claim (for v2 tokens). If the 'ver' claim is not present, it will first attempt to find the appId in the 'appid' claim and if not found, it will look in the 'azp' claim. Returns null if no suitable claim is found.
member.remarks: This is intended for use with tokens issued by the Microsoft identity platform including Azure Bot Token Service.
member.param: The JWT token to evaluate. Cannot be null.
member.returns: The appid or azp value as a string, or null if not found.

member.summary: "azp" Claim.

member.name: F:Microsoft.Agents.Authentication.AuthenticationConstants.AudienceClaim
member.summary: Audience Claim.
member.remarks:
The "aud" (audience) claim identifies the recipients that the JWT is intended for. Each principal intended to process the JWT MUST identify itself with a value in the audience claim. If the principal processing the claim does not identify itself with a value in the "aud" claim when this claim is present, then the JWT MUST be rejected. In the general case, the "aud" value is an array of case- sensitive strings, each containing a StringOrURI value. In the special case when the JWT has one audience, the "aud" value MAY be a single case-sensitive string containing a StringOrURI value. The interpretation of audience values is generally application specific. Use of this claim is OPTIONAL.
For more details, see RFC 7519 Section 4.1.3.

member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.Authentication.IAgenticTokenProvider
member.summary: Provides access tokens for the agentic identity chain used by Agent 365 / Agent ID scenarios.

remarks.para: Agentic identity is a layered model in which each token in the chain is used to acquire the next:

item.description: Application (blueprint) — a token-exchange credential bound to the agent application instance (the federated managed identity). Acquired via .
Instance — an autonomous-agent token, obtained by exchanging the application token. Acquired via or its scoped overload.
Agentic user — a token that represents the agent acting on behalf of a specific agentic user. Acquired via .

remarks.para: Implementations resolve this chain differently. The MSAL-based provider performs each exchange locally (using api://AzureAdTokenExchange/.default and federated managed identity / FMI paths), while the Entra Auth Sidecar provider delegates the full chain to an external sidecar process that owns the agent credential. A connection-level token provider exposes this interface when it supports agentic flows; callers typically obtain it through AgenticAuthorization.
